title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Handling of Petition Cases Related to Enforcement by People's Courts
keywords_en: People's Court handling enforcement petition cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Enforcement Petition Letters and Visits by People's Courts

Fa Fa [2016] No. 15

In order to implement the guiding spirit of the Central Committee on incorporating litigation-related petitions into the legal track, implementing the separation of litigation and petition, and establishing a sound termination system for petitions, in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Civil Procedure Law") and relevant judicial interpretations, and in light of the actual circumstances of the enforcement work of people's courts, the following opinions are hereby proposed regarding several issues such as the assignment and supervision of enforcement petition cases, the separation of litigation and petition, and the termination of petitions:

I. Basic Requirements for Handling Enforcement Petition Cases

1. Enforcement petition cases refer to cases in which a petitioner submits a petition to a people's court, requesting supervision over enforcement or correction of enforcement errors. Enforcement petition cases are divided into two categories: enforcement implementation-type petition cases and enforcement review-type petition cases.

2. The enforcement departments of people's courts at all levels shall establish specialized institutions for enforcement petitions; the reception and handling, assignment and supervision, as well as the review, submission, decision, and filing for record of the termination of petitions for enforcement petition cases shall be managed centrally by the enforcement departments of people's courts at all levels.

3. People's courts at all levels shall establish and improve the mechanism for handling enforcement petition cases, ensure unimpeded channels for enforcement-related petitions, and effectively disclose the handling procedures and results of petitions, to ensure that relevant requests are handled lawfully, promptly, and transparently:

(1) Establish a reception window for enforcement-related petition visits, publish a mailing address for enforcement-related petition letters, and assign personnel to receive visits and handle letters;

(2) After receiving petition materials, they shall promptly assign them to lower-level people's courts through the network system, internal correspondence, or other means;

(3) Notify the petitioner of the case processing progress and results by written notice or other appropriate means.

4. People's courts at all levels shall establish network systems for enforcement-related petitions such as online petition and remote video visits, guide petitioners to report issues through the network, and reduce traditional in-person or letter-based petitions.

5. People's courts at all levels shall establish and implement a system for the assignment and supervision of enforcement petition cases:

(1) After the higher-level people's court assigns an enforcement petition case, it shall further supervise the handling through effective working methods such as listed supervision, circuit supervision, and leadership responsibility for the case;

(2) Set up a ledger for enforcement petition cases, using the total number of enforcement petition cases and the number of resolved petition cases as the base, and using the case-to-petition ratio and resolution rate as indicators, and regularly circulate a notice to the courts within its jurisdiction;

(3) Include the enforcement petition work of courts within its jurisdiction in performance evaluation, and request the local Party committee's political and legal affairs commission to include it in the scope of assessment for comprehensive social management;

(4) If a lower-level people's court fails to implement the supervision opinions or the petition resolution work lags behind for a long time, the higher-level people's court may interview the deputy president in charge or the head of the enforcement bureau of the lower-level people's court, issue admonitions, and propose rectification requirements.

II. Handling of Enforcement Implementation-Type Petition Cases

6. Enforcement implementation-type petition cases refer to cases in which the enforcement applicant submits a petition, reporting the enforcement court's passive enforcement, and requesting supervision over enforcement.

The handling of enforcement implementation-type petition cases shall follow the principle of "completion of enforcement and effective resolution." If the enforcement respondent has property available for enforcement, all enforcement measures shall be exhausted to complete enforcement as soon as possible. If the enforcement respondent truly has no property available for enforcement, all efforts shall be made to explain and persuade, striving for withdrawal of the lawsuit and petition, and effectively resolving the petition contradiction; if after explanation and persuasion, the party still repeatedly petitions, persists in petitioning, or engages in disruptive petitioning, the petition may be terminated according to law.

7. An enforcement implementation-type petition case may be deemed as effectively resolved, and the higher-level people's court shall no longer assign or supervise, under the following circumstances:

(1) The case has indeed been fully enforced;

(2) The parties have reached an enforcement settlement agreement and have begun actual performance in accordance with the agreement;

(3) After re-investigation, the enforcement respondent truly has no property available for enforcement, and after explanation and persuasion or after the provision of judicial relief in accordance with relevant regulations, the enforcement applicant has made a written commitment to withdraw the lawsuit and petition.

8. If an enforcement applicant submits a petition requesting supervision over enforcement, the higher-level people's court shall no longer assign or supervise it as an enforcement petition case under the following circumstances:

(1) Enforcement has been suspended due to the acceptance of a bankruptcy petition, and the enforcement applicant has been notified to declare claims according to law;

(2) Enforcement has been suspended by a retrial ruling, and the enforcement applicant has been notified to participate in the proceedings according to law;

(3) Due to involvement in a crime, the case has been suspended according to relevant regulations and transferred to the relevant authority for handling;

(4) The petition request is based on the belief that the enforcement basis is erroneous.

9. If a case has been fully enforced, but the enforcement applicant submits a petition on the ground that the case has not been fully enforced, a notice of case closure shall be issued, and the party shall be informed of the right to raise an enforcement objection against the notice of case closure.

10. If the enforcement respondent truly has no property available for enforcement, and the enforcement court makes a ruling to terminate the current enforcement procedure in accordance with relevant regulations, and the enforcement applicant submits a petition on the ground that the case has not been fully enforced, the party shall be informed of the right to raise an enforcement objection against the ruling to terminate the current enforcement procedure.

III. Handling of Enforcement Review-Type Petition Cases

11. Enforcement review-type petition cases refer to cases in which a petitioner submits a petition, reporting that the enforcement act violates legal provisions or asserting substantive rights over the subject matter of enforcement, and requesting correction of enforcement errors.

The handling of enforcement review-type petition cases shall follow the principle of "separation of litigation and petition." If relief is available through the Civil Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations, the case must be reviewed through legal procedures; if all legal relief procedures and the enforcement supervision procedures provided for in these Opinions have been exhausted, and the party still repeatedly petitions, persists in petitioning, or engages in disruptive petitioning, the petition may be terminated according to law. If the matter falls within the scope of trial procedures or state compensation procedures, the party shall be informed to seek relief through the corresponding procedures.

12. If a petitioner requests the enforcement court to correct an enforcement error, and the matter meets the acceptance conditions for an enforcement objection or a third-party objection, the court shall accept it as a formal case under the case filing registration system for review.

13. If a petitioner does not submit a "Written Application for Enforcement Objection" to the enforcement court but asserts that the enforcement act violates legal provisions or asserts substantive rights over the subject matter of enforcement in forms such as a "Petition Letter" or "Status Report," the submission shall be treated as an application for enforcement objection and shall be accepted.

14. If a petitioner submits a petition to a higher-level people's court, asserting that the enforcement act of a lower-level people's court violates legal provisions or asserting substantive rights over the subject matter of enforcement, and the case has not yet been processed through the objection procedure or the enforcement supervision procedure, the higher-level people's court generally shall not conduct substantive review and shall handle it as follows:

(1) Inform the petitioner to seek relief in accordance with relevant regulations;

(2) Assign and supervise the case through the petition system, and order the lower-level people's court to review it through the objection procedure or the enforcement supervision procedure;

(3) After the lower-level people's court formally accepts the case for review, the higher-level people's court shall no longer assign or supervise.

15. If a party or interested party disagrees with the enforcement reconsideration ruling as provided for in Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law and submits a petition to the people's court at the next higher level, the court at the next higher level shall accept the case as an enforcement supervision case for review and reach a conclusion by ruling.

16. If a party or interested party has already raised an objection within the objection period, but the enforcement court did not accept and review the case, and the party or interested party continues to submit a petition after the expiration of the objection period, the enforcement court shall accept the case as an enforcement supervision case for review and reach a conclusion by ruling.

If a party or interested party disagrees with the enforcement supervision ruling provided for in the preceding paragraph and continues to submit a petition to the people's court at the next higher level, the court at the next higher level shall accept the case as an enforcement supervision case for review and reach a conclusion by ruling.

17. If a petitioner submits a petition to a higher-level people's court, reporting that an objection or reconsideration case has seriously exceeded the trial duration, the higher-level people's court shall assign and supervise the case through the petition system, ordering the lower-level people's court to issue an objection or reconsideration ruling within a specified time limit.

18. If a party or interested party submits a petition requesting correction of an enforcement error, the higher-level people's court shall no longer assign or supervise it as an enforcement petition case under the following circumstances:

(1) The petition request is directed at a ruling of approval of enforcement made by the people's court upon application by an administrative authority, rather than at the enforcement act;

(2) The petition request is based on the belief that the enforcement basis is erroneous.

IV. Lawful Termination of Enforcement Petition Cases

19. If the enforcement respondent truly has no property available for enforcement, and the enforcement applicant has made a written commitment to withdraw the lawsuit and petition, but subsequently repeatedly petitions, persists in petitioning, or engages in disruptive petitioning on the same grounds, the enforcement court may report level by level to the higher-level people's court to decide on the termination of the petition.

20. If a party or interested party raises an enforcement objection, and after review through the objection procedure, reconsideration procedure, and enforcement supervision procedure, the final conclusion denies its request, and the party still repeatedly petitions, persists in petitioning, or engages in disruptive petitioning, the petition may be terminated according to law:

(1) If the enforcement supervision ruling was made by a higher-level people's court, the higher-level people's court shall decide on the termination of the petition;

(2) If the enforcement reconsideration or supervision ruling was made by the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Court shall decide on the termination of the petition or refer it to the higher-level people's court for termination.

21. For an enforcement implementation-type petition case, even if the petition has been terminated, the enforcement court shall still periodically inquire about the property status of the enforcement respondent; if the enforcement applicant provides new property leads and requests resumption of enforcement, the enforcement court shall immediately resume enforcement.

22. If the enforcement applicant suffers severe hardship in life due to the failure to enforce the case, the petition shall generally not be terminated.

23. Before a higher-level people's court decides to terminate a petition, it shall report to the Supreme People's Court for record. If the Supreme People's Court finds that the conditions are not met, it shall promptly notify the higher-level people's court to make corrections or return the case. If the record is not approved for termination, the higher-level people's court shall not terminate.

24. If the Supreme People's Court or a higher-level people's court decides to terminate a petition, it shall notify the petitioner in writing.

25. For an enforcement petition case that has been terminated, except as otherwise provided, the higher-level people's court shall no longer assign or supervise, and people's courts at all levels shall not conduct repeated review; after the petition is terminated, if the petitioner still repeatedly petitions, persists in petitioning, or engages in disruptive petitioning, it shall be handled in a timely manner according to law, and the local Party committee's political and legal affairs commission shall be informed.

26. Other procedural requirements for the termination of enforcement petitions shall be handled in accordance with the relevant regulations on the termination of civil case petitions.
